title: It is false that: A step toward: Petersen graph: some circuit with at most 6 AND gates, ORs free, is correct on its partial function with each… (step 1 of 3)
formal_statement: ¬ (have x1 : ℕ → Finset (Fin (10 : ℕ)) := fun (x1 : ℕ) => {x2 : Fin (10 : ℕ) | x1.testBit ↑x2 = Bool.true}; have x2 : List ℕ := [(50 : ℕ), (69 : ℕ), (104 : ℕ), (116 : ℕ), (138 : ℕ), (201 : ℕ), (208 : ℕ), (276 : ℕ), (385 : ℕ), (402 : ℕ), (521 : ℕ), (548 : ℕ), (554 : ℕ), (770 : ℕ), (773 : ℕ)]; ∃ (x3 : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit (10 : ℕ)),   x3.WellFormed ∧     x3.size ≤ (6 : ℕ) ∧       (∀ (x4 : Fin (10 : ℕ)),           have x5 : Finset (Fin x3.size) := {x5 : Fin x3.size | x4 ∈ x3.leftVars x5 ∨ x4 ∈ x3.rightVars x5};           x5.card ≤ (2 : ℕ)) ∧         ∀ x4 ∈ x2, x3.eval (x1 x4) = Bool.false ∧ ((x1 x4).card = (3 : ℕ) → ∀ x7 ∉ x1 x4, x3.eval (Insert.insert x7 (x1 x4)) = Bool.true))
plain_statement: It is false that: There is an AND-count circuit on the Petersen graph's 10 vertices (AND gates of two OR-sides, the output an OR; only AND gates counted) with at most 6 AND gates, each vertex bare in at most two gates, false at each of 15 listed vertex sets, and true at each listed set of three vertices once any further vertex is added.
